explanation: A11.5 item 2 treats production use of `prototype/policy-signer/` as the path needing no ruling, but the prototype is instrument code by A9.2's location rule ("it lives under `prototype/` … and service code never imports it", A9:198-199), which the opening record lets reach production only as a port earning fresh evidence — and A11 itself says the 21 Oct qualification "does not qualify a replacement", which a port would be. why.claude: A11's fallback runs production through prototype/policy-signer/, while FREEZE-RECORD says "Instrument code under prototype/ stays instrument code" and A9.2 says instrument output never stands as evidence. But the frozen profile itself names that implementation for production custody, so the texts don't settle whether this is barred.

explanation: With the parameters A9.2 ratifies (δ = 72 h, S = 24 h, A9:223), the registered attempt lifecycle runs 96 hours from declaration and A2.1 makes 'every timely-eligible attempt ships' a contract obligation on the implementation; the owner service resolution terminates every request at 24 hours, so the same honest request whose anchor confirms between 24 and 96 hours is shippable under one rule and terminally FAILED under the other. The resolutions are 'stamped but not registered' (A11.5 item 2) and A11's dependency sweep did not flag them against the registered attempt lifecycle.

why.claude: A2.1/A2.3 have the service wait through declared + δ + S (96 h at A9.2's values) and make "every timely-eligible attempt ships" a contract obligation; the owner resolution ends any request not complete 24 h after acceptance as FAILED, so a timely-eligible attempt confirming after 24 h cannot ship.
why.codex: A2 requires waiting through “declared + δ + S” before expiry, with δ=72h and S=24h. S4 instead ends every unfinished accepted request after “24 hours”, without reconciling the registered attempt lifecycle.

explanation: The rationale for rule O's header names GnuPG as 'the gpg signer'. The slot-2 custody decision replaced it with a GCP HSM behind a policy signer that builds its own packet, so the sentence's referent changed and was not re-read.

explanation: A9 establishes authority at the channels' evidence times rather than at issue time. Its change table does not list A1's stronger issue-time assertion.

why.codex: W1 says the anchor digest “is not an identifier”; §9 says a receipt’s identity “is SHA256(A_sig)” and directs deduplication by it. The unqualified identifier prohibition conflicts with that express identity rule.

explanation: The profile requires reading fingerprint bytes to check their version and consistency with the issuer key ID. PROOF retains the broader assertion that no V1 check reads those bytes, rather than merely saying they confer no key-binding authority.

why.codex: PROOF says “no V1 check reads” the issuer-fingerprint bytes, but the profile requires their version, length and consistency checks. Lack of key-selection authority does not mean the bytes are unread.
